src/mlframe/feature_selection/filters/_u: The per-fold loop runs over nf folds, a fixed small count, and each fold's bordered systems are already batched over the candidates. Batching over the folds too was measured (scratchpad cv_block_bench, RTX 500 Ada): 2x faster at n=6000 (sel=0 24.1 -> 12.4 ms, sel=2 34.7 -> 16.6 ms) but 4-9x slower at n=40000 (sel=0 13.9 -> 80-125 ms, sel=2 39.0 -> 143-185 ms), because the stacked (nf, n, m) tensors cost more than the per-fold (n, m) work. Rejected; the loop stays.
src/mlframe/feature_selection/filters/_p: The loop runs over the distinct effective bin counts max(nbins, modulus), one group per distinct count (1 with the default moduli at small nbins, up to about 8 with COARSE_MODULI). Each group needs its own interior quantile edges, which depend on its bin count, so the edges stay one radix selection per group. The MI itself is one fused call per chunk (_grid_block_one_call); this loop is the fallback when the fused tile does not fit. Measured: 2 groups at n=40000 9.7 -> 6.4 ms; at n=6000 no gain.

Same loop as combiner_bases_and_grids_resident: one iteration per distinct effective bin count, building that group's residues and interior edges (per-group radix selection, see the combiner entry). The MI of all groups is a single fused call; the loop only gathers the per-group edges and residues.
src/mlframe/feature_selection/filters/_r: The loop runs once per distinct operand count (arity) of the operand sets in a block, which is 2 and 3 in the search. Each arity has its own candidate-row layout (k = m + 4*pairs + 2 + sum), so the sets of different arities cannot share one launch without padding the candidate rows. Within an arity all sets are built by one set-batched kernel and written with one row scatter, which replaced one builder launch per set (measured: 64 pair sets at n=40000 went from 17.3 ms to 9.2 ms; the per-set builder alone was 15.5 ms). Bit-identical to the per-set builder, including NaN operands (checked on mixed arities).
src/mlframe/feature_selection/filters/_u: The numpy reference of the logit null: its Newton loop is a fixed 6 to 8 steps over (rows, candidates, draws) arrays and is only ever run with xp=numpy (the unit tests compare the njit twin and the fused device kernel logit_null_loglik with it); the device route is that one fused kernel, one launch for every candidate and draw (record _unary_credit_logit_cuda.md), so no launch-bound cupy loop is reachable here.

The loops run over at most MAX_COLUMNS = 30 numeric columns and the credit passes. Each column's test conditions on the current design of the other columns, which the previous column's verdict may have changed within the pass, so the columns are sequential by construction; one column costs one fused-kernel null (1 to 3 launches) and the whole credit stage 0.6 s at 100000 x 100 (ledger led100m, 2026-11-24).
src/mlframe/feature_selection/filters/_m: The flagged loop is the error walk over the at most four stage outcomes: nothing happens for a stage without an error, and the first failing stage raises after merging the stages before it, so the cupy comparison inside merge_stage_state (_same on device arrays) runs once, on the failure path only. The success path merges once, outside the loop; there is no per-iteration launch to batch.
